main_issue: Whether Agent D should do their unfinished pitch section alone tonight (with a grandmother's burial today) or whether teammates should help; who covers the work before Thursday.

A-B.evidence: A proposes B, C and A help finish D's section (12); B declines, covering for someone on leave (13). B takes no position on D's plan, and A accepts the situation.

A-C.evidence: Both worry about D's capacity (5, 7) and press for a timing (9, 10). C declines A's help request (15), but both end worried and with no alternative (36-38).

A-D.evidence: A questions whether D can work tonight and offers to take over (5, 12). D insists on doing it alone (16). A concedes: 'Okay, Agent D. If you're sure. We'll be counting on you' (17), though A remains worried (37).

B-C.evidence: B speaks only once, to decline (13). C also declines (15), a parallel stance, but they never address each other.

B-D.evidence: B says only that they can't help (13) and never addresses D's plan. D never responds to B.

C-D.evidence: C doubts D can manage it (7) and asks when it will arrive (9). D insists they'll deliver (8, 11). C ends hoping D can do it (36) but stays worried.
